BREAKING: Palantir's Alex Karp says OpenAl will never IPO.
X
His theory: nationalization is the only real exit.
When asked what the S-1 risk factors look like, Karp's answer was simple: there is no S-1.
The liability exposure from frontier Al is so large that no public market can absorb it.
The only entity big enough to backstop it is a government.
If Karp is right, OpenAl doesn't become the next Google.
It becomes a utility. Or a weapon.
The most valuable Al company in the world may have no clean path to public markets.
Is nationalization actually the most likely outcome for frontier Al labs?

Open-weight typed decisions on Apple Silicon. Core ML, Neural Engine, zero generated tokens.

PyPI · Hugging Face weights · 中文

A real Laya model plays Snake locally, with visible probabilities, score, length, latency and safety interventions. The GIF replays a recorded Core ML run at 1× speed. The game uses explicit planner features and a visible cycle safety layer.

The complete active Snake loop sustained 49.1–50.0 decisions/s across three uncapped 600-step episodes, with zero deaths and two safety interventions. Game-loop timings and paced-rate limits include rendering serialization; terminal painting is excluded.

One short multilingual decision: 4.98 ms P50 / 5.31 ms P95 on M3 Max with ANE FP16. The same experiment measured 2.78× better whole-system energy per decision than compiled MLX FP16. A separately validated W8 palette variant reached 4.88 ms and 3.19× energy improvement. These are single-question results, not full Snake frame times; the requested 10× improvement was not achieved.

Amazon says it has cut off Meta's new Muse personal Al agent from shopping on Amazon.com on behalf of customers, after attempting unsuccessfully to get the Facebook parent company to voluntarily exclude the e-commerce site from the experience.
The problem, Amazon says, is that it never agreed to any of it. Meta didn't tell Amazon that Muse would access its store, the agent doesn't identify itself when it browses, and it appears to capture and store customer credentials, which the company says could create privacy and security risks.
As of Sunday night, people trying to use Muse to shop on Amazon were seeing the popup, "Continued access by an unauthorized Al agent violates Amazon's Conditions of Use, to which our customers have agreed."

A line chart comparing AI model performance on the "CursorBench 4.0 score" (y-axis, ranging from 20% to 55%) relative to the "Average cost per task" (x-axis, inverted scale from $18 down to $0).
The chart plots five models:
 * Fable 5.1 (gold line): Scores highest overall, ranging from ~52% at $17.50 down to ~45% at $5.
 * Opus 5 (light blue line): Ranges from ~46% score at $12 down to ~41% at $5.
 * Grok 4.7 (black line): Ranges from ~46% score at $6 down to ~33% at $1.50.
 * GPT-5.6 Sol (pink line with a highlighted red dot): Ranges from ~42% score at $8 down to ~24% at $0.80, with a red marker at ~$1.80 and 31% score.
 * Sonnet 5 (green line): Ranges from ~34% score at $7 down to ~24% at $1.20.
Across all models, benchmark scores decline as the average cost per task approaches $0.
